title: Interactive safe-failback policy and targeted patch-branch strategy for LTS and rolling channels
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: define a pragmatic, auditable hotfix + failback flow that covers both LTS and rolling releases; codify severity thresholds, branch naming and backport rules; implement lightweight automation for safe cherry-picks and fast canary failbacks. Scope includes: severity matrix, patch-branch topology, automated backport bot behavior, rollout gate criteria, observability checks for abort/failback, and on-call responsibilities. Out of scope: large-scale database migrations and CI-level image rebuild tooling (handled in ENG-558901).
acceptance_criteria: A documented severity matrix with examples and SLO thresholds published in Confluence
Branching convention defined and enforced by CI (hotfix branch creation and protected branch rules)
Backport automation (backport-bot) can create candidate PRs for 2 supported backport channels (LTS and maintenance)
Rollout gated canary pipeline with automated health checks can trigger an automated failback within 10 minutes
Runbook for emergency hotpatch includes clear owner handoff, Slack escalation play, and postmortem template
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: On-call posts incident to #releases and tags release-engineering; assign severity using table below
2) Hotfix branch: create branch hotfix/<semver>-<short-key> (example: hotfix/2.4.3-ENG-241309) from the branch matching the target release channel
3) Patch PR: open PR to target branch and add label backport-request to trigger backport-bot for secondary channels
4) QA Canary: promote to canary cluster with 1% traffic for 10m and run canary checks (latency p95, error-rate, key end-to-end tests), see gating thresholds
5) Promote or Failback: if canary passes, progressive rollout 10% -> 25% -> 100% with 15m observation windows; if any window violates thresholds, run automated failback action
6) Backporting: backport-bot opens candidate PRs; release engineer reviews and merges after CI green and owner sign-off
7) Postmortem: complete postmortem within 72 hours with root cause, timeline, and follow-ups
severity_matrix: Severity 1 (SEV1): production-wide data corruption, P0. Immediate hotpatch permitted. Failback within 10m if regression observed.
Severity 2 (SEV2): degraded performance or partial outage affecting >25% of customers, P0/P1. Hotfix allowed; use canary + short rollout windows.
Severity 3 (SEV3): minor feature regressions or isolated errors, P2. Defer to next micro-patch unless customer-impacting.
Severity definitions include concrete metrics: error-rate delta >1.5x baseline or absolute error-rate >0.5% (SEV2/SEV1 thresholds) and p95 latency increase >20%
branching_policy: Source branches: rolling releases fork from main; LTS branches named release/2.4.x; hotfixes must be created from the branch that matches the customer-facing release
Protection: hotfix branches are protected; PRs require 1 owner approval + CI passing; release engineers can bypass for SEV1 with documented reason
Backport targets: primary branch (release/2.4.x) and secondary maintenance (release/2.3.x) depending on CVE/impact matrix
backport_tooling: backport-bot: listens for label backport-request and attempts automated cherry-picks into configured targets
Conflict handling: candidate PR is opened and assigned to the original author and release engineer; backport-bot annotates conflicts with suggested commands
Manual fallback: if cherry-pick fails, release engineer creates manual branch with explicit cherry-pick and documents the steps in the PR
Audit trail: every backport PR must include the original PR reference and a small changelog entry for compliance
gating_criteria: Canary windows: 10m observation at 1% traffic with automatic checks
Success thresholds: no increase in error-rate >0.5 percentage points OR >1.5x baseline and p95 latency regression <10%
Alerting: auto-trigger if observability signals breach thresholds; automatic rollback initiated unless manual override from release lead
Manual hold: release lead may pause rollout between windows for investigation; hold should have explicit next-check ETA
operational_playbook_notes: On-call role: Release Engineer (RE) is responsible for branch creation and coordination; SRE supports canary/metrics
Escalation matrix: RE -> Release Manager -> Head of Platform for SEV1 decisions
Post-release audit: CI job collects rollout telemetry to release-audit bucket for 90 days
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Platform, and PM. Agreed to support 2 backport channels (LTS + maintenance). Action: prototype backport-bot (Luca)
2026-02-27: Prototype backport-bot created (internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/backport-bot/pull/9). Bot creates candidate PRs and labels them.
2026-03-03: Draft gating thresholds reviewed by SRE; adjusted p95 threshold from 15% to 10% after load-test results. See doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Hotfix+gating+thresholds
2026-03-07: Runbook draft reviewed in staging incident drill; automated failback tested successfully in simulation (rollback executed within 6m).
2026-03-10: Created protection rules in GitHub (branch protection + required checks). Preparing checklist for SEV1 bypass flow and audit recording.
open_questions: What exact permission set should a release engineer have for SEV1 bypass to balance speed vs auditability? (options: temporary token vs explicit PR approval log)
Should we include an automated rollback-only label that triggers a higher-privilege path and records an auditable reason?
How many historical minor versions do we guarantee backports for before we mark 'end-of-maintenance' for an LTS line?
